correctness.rationale: For k>=3 and n>=2k, a 2k-incidence witness colors the endpoints of one deleted matching pair with every color. If weight<2k, each n-vertex shore contains an empty vertex and hence each opposite shore must carry at least k color incidences: contradiction. At weight 2k, when both shores contain empties, each color occurs once per shore and an empty matched partner forces identical index supports; two independent surjections onto common T exhaust all cases. When one entire shore is occupied, equality forces n=2k, singleton labels on all its vertices and twice each color. Counts by Stirling surjections and permutations follow bijectively. Independent new enumeration of all incidence subsets of weight<=6 found 1,446 valid functions among 2,391,496 for (k,n)=(3,6) and 2,023 among 6,220,768 for (3,7), with no smaller-weight case; finite tests only supplement the universal proof.
